import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
data = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv',
                   index_col=False,
                   dtype={'model_year': 'int64',
                          'megapixels': 'float64',
                          'max_iso': 'int64',
                          'weight_grams': 'int64',
                          'price_usd': 'float64',
                          'has_video_4k': 'int64'})

# Plot a bar chart to compare the number of cameras with different sensor types
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.countplot(x='sensor_type', data=data)
plt.title('Number of Cameras by Sensor Type')
plt.xlabel('Sensor Type')
plt.ylabel('Count')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Plot a scatter plot to show the relationship between megapixels and price
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.scatterplot(x='megapixels', y='price_usd', data=data)
plt.title('Relationship between Megapixels and Price')
plt.xlabel('Megapixels')
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Plot a histogram to show the distribution of camera weights
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.histplot(data['weight_grams'], kde=True)
plt.title('Distribution of Camera Weights')
plt.xlabel('Weight (grams)')
plt.ylabel('Count')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Plot a bar chart to compare the number of cameras with and without 4K video capabilities
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.countplot(x='has_video_4k', data=data)
plt.title('Number of Cameras with 4K Video Capabilities')
plt.xlabel('4K Video Capabilities')
plt.ylabel('Count')
plt.legend(title='4K Video Capabilities')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
